title: Kwai Summary Attention V2 Technical Report
summary: KSA V2 replaces rigid same-window summary-token interleaving with summary tokens that act both as KV memory and sparse indexers, allowing per-layer compression windows and cheaper full-attention layers. It costs architectural modification and training from scratch or substantial fine-tuning, plus added serving complexity in the KV cache path, with unverified quality at long contexts. It can fail through degraded recall of distant exact content under aggressive per-layer compression and through implementation mismatch with standard inference stacks.
rationale: Because it requires training a custom attention architecture and custom KV cache handling, a team with one GPU or API-only access cannot adopt it now, but the dual-role summary token idea is worth tracking for future open-weight releases.
technique: Hybrid summary-token attention with per-layer compression (KSA V2)
